The defaults are provisional and are tuned as the renderer is measured, so do not assert against a shipped number.

— the detent of a classic mouse wheel, which the browser reports as about 100 pixels of
takes roughly five notches to double the zoom; raise it for a faster wheel, lower it for a slower one. Scrolling the other way applies the reciprocal, so a notch out undoes a notch in exactly.

, and there is deliberately no separate knob for one. A trackpad never emits a notch — it emits a stream of much smaller deltas — but because the rate underneath is per pixel, it covers the same 100 pixels over several events and gets the same zoom for the same scroll distance. Nothing in the viewer detects which device is in use; the usual heuristics are unreliable and that branch is a permanent source of hardware-specific bugs. If the trackpad feels different from the mouse, this single value moves both.
